task_instance: Set up TypeScript 7 quality gates (Oxlint-only lint + type diagnostics, Prettier format check, Knip dead-code, jscpd duplicates, a check.sh orchestrator, and prek pre-commit/pre-push hooks) on a small sample TypeScript project, and verify the canonical full gate passes.
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a working, verified quality gate: it explicitly states to count a configured gate as working only after it passes, and the install and verify steps require installing dev dependencies (TypeScript 7, oxlint, oxlint-tsgolint, knip, jscpd, prettier), installing the prek runner as a per-machine tool, marking check.sh executable, and executing the gate commands (oxlint --type-aware --type-check, oxlint --print-config, npm run scripts, and prek run --all-files --group full). The office-assistant runtime cannot run any code, scripts or shell commands, cannot install software, and cannot execute the configured tools, so none of the gates can be run or verified. I authored all required configuration files but could not produce or verify the actual working gate, which is the deliverable.
evidence: Read the skill document and references/orchestration.md from the skill repo. Built a minimal sample TypeScript project under the work directory at sample-app/ with: package.json (TS7 devDependencies and lint/format/deadcode/duplicates/check scripts), tsconfig.json, src/index.ts (small typed module), .oxlintrc.json (the skill's recommended correctness+policy ruleset), jscpd.json (duplicate policy), .pre-commit-config.yaml (typescript-fast/typescript-full hook split with fast and full/ci groups), and check.sh (the --fast/--full/--fix orchestrator from the skill's reference). These are configuration artifacts only. The gate cannot be realized or verified because every verification path requires code execution and package installation: cannot npm-install the toolchain, cannot install the prek runner, cannot chmod check.sh, and cannot run oxlint, tsc, knip, jscpd, or 'prek run --all-files --group full'. No model calls, web fetches, shell commands, or MCP/connector tools were used.
